_doc: #772 THE ONE declaration of image recognition, shared by every app that compiles this contract (Cloud Camera and Cloud Calc first): which routes exist, which is the default, the thresholds, the colour names, and the OpenRouter route's endpoint, model, categories and questions. libs:ml-l-image bakes it into BuildConfig (IMAGE_RECOGNITION_B64), RecognitionConfig reads it, and every recognize request carries the parts the engine needs, so the engine (Cloud-Lib-Ml-L-Image-Mlkit.apk) holds no copy of its own and an edit here re-ships the apps that show it. Per device, each app keeps only the user's route and model choice (RecognitionPrefs).
_doc_routes: ml = on-device ML Kit (image labelling, object detection with boxes, text recognition) plus ZXing barcodes and the dominant colours: fully offline, the default. openrouter = a decision model on OpenRouter's Decisions API (libs:decisions) asked one choice over `categories` plus the extra `questions`, the photo attached as an image part and the on-device colours as text: decision models answer with calibrated probabilities, mapped into the same labels/answers shape. When the OpenRouter route fails (no token, HTTP error, timeout) and fallback_to_ml is true, the on-device route answers and the result says fell_back with the reason. A model that cannot see images still answers, from the text part: that is why the colours ride along.
_doc_detect: #798 live identification (detect, contract 3): always on device, whatever the route, because a decision model per camera frame is neither offline nor fast. objects = ML Kit object detection with the engine's full-label classifier (1000 ImageNet classes), up to max_objects boxes each with labels_per_object labels at or above min_confidence, tracking ids in stream mode; labels = ML Kit image labelling of the whole frame (max_labels); text = one box per recognised line. A frame is sized to max_side before detection (live_side for a viewfinder frame, which is smaller so the round trip stays under a few hundred ms); interval_ms is the shortest gap between two live frames a caller sends. The user's route applies to the photo a snapshot saves, through recognize.

colours._doc_names: The vocabulary a dominant colour is named in: the nearest by the redmean distance. Hex values are sRGB.

openrouter.instructions: Which category best describes the main subject of this photo? The photo is attached when the model can see it; `measured` lists what the phone measured on-device (dominant colours) and any text the user added as `context`.

categories.object: A manufactured object, tool, device or household item.
categories.plant: A plant, flower, tree or leaves.
categories.food: Food, a dish, fruit or vegetables.
categories.vehicle: A car, bicycle, boat, plane or other vehicle.
categories.document: A document, sign, label, receipt or screen of text.
categories.material: A close-up of a material or texture: wood, fabric, stone, metal, plastic.
categories.landscape: A landscape, sky, water or outdoor scene.
categories.other: Something else, or too unclear to say.

text_present.label: Text present?
text_present.instructions: The photo shows readable text or numbers.

damaged.label: Damaged?
damaged.instructions: The main subject looks damaged, broken, worn or spoiled.

ripe.label: Ripe?
ripe.instructions: If the main subject is fruit or vegetables, how ripe is it?

criteria.not_produce: The subject is not fruit or vegetables.
